title: Muse voice gadget
purpose: An ESP32-S3 voice assistant for the Muse Gadgets SDK: round 1.28" screen on the back, I2S microphone and speaker amplifier, talk button; USB-C powered

source.title: muse-voice recipe
source.author: the circuit harness: Mitayi-Pico USB-C and LED blocks (CIRCUITSTATE, MIT), new blocks from Espressif, Diodes, TDK, Maxim and Waveshare documents; pins after the Muse Gadgets SDK's Guition and Waveshare board files
source.licence: MIT blocks; new blocks quote their datasheets

open_questions: Our own board_*.c for the Muse SDK is still to write: screen on IO9-IO14 (DIN, CLK, CS, DC, RST, BL), I2S BCLK IO42, WS IO39, amp IO41, mic IO40.

Power from USB at 5 V, peaks: ESP32 Wi-Fi TX 355 mA (wroom1 Table 6-4, through the linear regulator), amp about 240 mA at 1 W into 8 Ω (92% efficient, max98357a), backlight up to 45 mA, panel 10.5 mA: about 650 mA, over a USB 2.0 port's 500 mA but within a Type-C charger's 1.5 or 3 A. The input diode is rated 1.0 A. Speaker not chosen; an 8 Ω 1 W speaker keeps within this.
Display: see the round display block's questions; the mic's sound hole is outside the panel.
